classification.habit: Diffuse perennial herb with tuberous root
classification.habitat: Waste lands, roadsides, fields and sandy soils, flourishing after the rainy season.
classification.distribution: Throughout India as a common weed, from the plains up to about 2000 m.

identification.description: Diffusely branched perennial herb with stout root, green upper leaf surface, pale/whitish lower surface and small pinkish-red flowers.
identification.whole_plant: Diffusely branched, trailing perennial herb with a stout tuberous root-stock and long slender prostrate or ascending branches.
identification.root: Well developed, fairly long, somewhat tortuous, cylindrical, 0.2–1.5 cm thick, yellowish-brown to brown, with longitudinal striations; fracture short; taste slightly bitter.
identification.stem: Greenish-purple, slender, cylindrical, swollen at nodes, minutely pubescent, divaricately branched, often over a metre long.
identification.leaf: Opposite in unequal pairs, ovate-oblong to suborbicular, green and glabrous above, whitish below, margin entire or wavy, petiole nearly as long as the blade.
identification.flower: Very small pink flowers in small umbels on long slender stalks; perianth tube constricted above the ovary, upper part funnel-shaped; stamens 2–3.
identification.fruit: One-seeded clavate anthocarp, about 6 mm long, bluntly 5-ribbed and viscid-glandular.
identification_points: Prostrate herb with purple, node-swollen stems
Opposite leaves in unequal pairs, whitish beneath
Minute pink flowers in umbels on long stalks

therapeutics.dose: Churna (root) 1–3 g; Kwatha: 20–30 g drug for decoction
therapeutics.precautions: Strongly diuretic; monitor fluid and electrolyte status in long use, and do not replace medical evaluation of oedema, ascites or kidney disease.
therapeutics.contraindications: Pregnancy (in medicinal doses) and severe dehydration; caution with concurrent diuretic or antihypertensive medicines.

shlokas:
पुनर्नवा श्वेतमूला शोथघ्नी दीर्घपत्रिका ।
कटुकषायानुरसा पाण्डुघ्नी दीपनी परा ।
शोफानिलगरश्लेष्महरी व्रण्योदरप्रणुत् ॥

phytochemistry.chemical_notes: API lists the alkaloid punarnavine; rotenoids (boeravinones) and potassium salts are also reported and contribute to the diuretic profile.

modern_information.evidence_summary: Known for its diuretic and rejuvenating properties, Punarnava supports kidney and liver function and reduces swelling.
recognized_uses: Leafy vegetable in parts of India
modern_information.safety_notes: Generally well tolerated in traditional doses; its diuretic effect may add to that of prescribed diuretics.
